chapter.chapter: Chapter 7 — Work, Energy, and Simple Machines

excerpts:
[INJSO 2009 — question paper]
1. Which one of the following expressions has the same units as power?
a) Force x distance
b) Work x time
¢) Force x acceleration
d) Force x velocity

[INJSO 2010 — question paper]
46. A trolley runs from point P to Q along a track, as shown in the figure. At point Q,
its potential energy is 50 kJ less than at point P. At point P, the trolley has kinetic energy
5 kJ. Between P and Q, the work done against friction is 10 kJ. What is the kinetic energy
at point Q?
a) 35 kJ b) 45 kJ c) 55 kJ d) 65 kJ

[INJSO 2012 — question paper]
1. A load is to be moved using a wheelbarrow. The total mass of the load and wheelbarrow is 60 kg.
The magnitude of gravitational acceleration is 10 ms 2 .
What is the work done if the handle is raised by 50 cm?
a) 35.0 J
b) 17.5 J
c) 175 J
d) 350 J

[INJSO 2012 — question paper]
45. The diagram shows a lift system in which the elevator (mass m 1 ) is partly counterbalanced by a
heavy weight (mass m 2 ).
At what rate does the motor provide energy to the system when the elevator is rising at a steady
speed v ? (g = acceleration of free fall) (consider the pulley as frictionless at the pivot)
a) (m 1 + m 2 )gv
b) ½ (m 1 + m 2 )gv
c) (m 1 m 2 )gv /(m 1 + m 2 )
d) (m 1 – m 2 )gv

items.stem: In the graph shown in Fig. 7.4, the force on an object is plotted on the Y-axis against the displacement on the X-axis. What does the area of the shaded rectangle represent?
If a force of 10 N is applied to move an object by 2 m in the direction of the force, what is the work done?
Which of the following is the SI unit of work?

When a force is applied perpendicular to the direction of displacement, what is the work done by the force?
A force of 10 N is applied on an object, but it does not move. What is the work done in this case?
A goalkeeper stops a ball by moving her hand back by 15 cm while applying a force of 200 N. What is the work done by the goalkeeper on the ball?

A trolley moves from point P to point Q. Its potential energy decreases by 50 kJ, and the work done against friction is 10 kJ. The trolley has 5 kJ of kinetic energy at P. What is its kinetic energy at Q?
A lift system has an elevator of mass m1 and a counterweight of mass m2. It moves upward at a steady speed v. What is the rate at which the motor provides energy to the system?
Which of the following is an example of negative work done?
When you pedal a bicycle on a flat road, your muscles supply energy. In what forms does this muscular energy appear as you ride?

A jet aircraft of mass 15000 kg lands on the deck of an aircraft carrier and is stopped within 100 m by a wire that exerts a force of 367500 N. What was the velocity of the aircraft just before the wire caught the hook?

A trolley runs from point P to Q along a track. Its potential energy at Q is 50 kJ less than at P, and its kinetic energy at P is 5 kJ. Between P and Q, the work done against friction is 10 kJ. What is the kinetic energy at Q?
A carrom striker hits a white coin, which then hits a black coin. What kind of work does the striker do on the white coin?
A lift system has an elevator of mass m₁ and a counterweight of mass m₂. What is the rate at which the motor provides energy to the system when the elevator is rising at a steady speed v?
When a ball is dropped from a greater height, it creates a deeper depression in the sand. Why does this happen?
A ball is raised to a height of 2 m and released. The work done in lifting the ball is 100 J. What is the gravitational potential energy of the ball at this height?
What is the unit of potential energy?
What is the main conclusion from the passage about the potential energy of the student when lifted or climbing the stairs?
If a crane lifts a mass m to the 10th floor in a certain time, and then lifts the same mass to the 20th floor in double the time, how much more energy and power are required?
In the passage, a ball is thrown up with a velocity of 20 m/s. If the ball reaches a height of 19.4 m, how much work was done by air resistance?
What is the velocity of a coconut just before it hits the sand, if it falls from a height of 10 m?

A man of mass 60 kg rides a scooter of mass 100 kg. He accelerates the scooter to a velocity v. The next day, his son with a mass of 40 kg joins him as a passenger. If the scooter reaches the same speed on both days in the same time interval, what is the ratio of the fuel used on the two days?
Which of the following is an example of a simple machine that reduces the force required to perform a task but does not reduce the total work done?

In the passage, a 10.0 kg block is moving on a horizontal floor with negligible friction. A variable force is applied on the block from 0 m to 4 m. The block had a kinetic energy of 180 J at 0 m. What is the speed of the block at 4 m?

In the given scenario, a seesaw is balanced with two children. One child has a mass of 15 kg and sits on seat A, which is 2 meters from the fulcrum. To balance the seesaw, where should a child of 30 kg sit?

A trolley moves from point P to Q along a track. At point P, the trolley has kinetic energy of 5 kJ. The potential energy at Q is 50 kJ less than at P. The work done against friction between P and Q is 10 kJ. What is the kinetic energy at Q?
What is the SI unit for both work and energy?
A cart is pulled up a ramp with a length of 5 m, and the height of the ramp is 3 m. The force required to pull the cart is 60 N. What is the work done in pulling the cart up the ramp?
A person lifts a box vertically and then uses an inclined plane to move the same box to the same height. Which of the following is true about the work done in both cases?
A box is pushed up a frictionless inclined plane. The height of the plane is 2 m and the length of the plane is 5 m. What is the mechanical advantage of the inclined plane?
A box is moved up a frictionless inclined plane of length L and height h. A force F is applied to move the box. According to the work-energy theorem, which of the following relationships is correct?
A force of 5 N is applied on an object, and it is displaced by 4 m in the direction of the force. What is the work done?
What is the SI unit of power?
What is the energy stored in a deformed object or in a system of objects due to their relative positions called?
What is the SI unit of power?
What is the main purpose of using an inclined plane to lift a heavy object?
What is the SI unit of kinetic energy?
If a lever is used to lift a load, and the effort arm is increased, what happens to the effort required?
A spring is compressed and then released. The spring transfers its stored energy to an object in contact. What is the source of the energy transferred to the object?
